title: Making complex CFTs real: The two-dimensional Potts model for $Q>4$ and complex $Q$
authors: Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, Kay Joerg Wiese
abstract: The two-dimensional $Q$-state Potts model with real couplings has a first-order transition for $Q>4$. Starting from a triangular-lattice Potts model with two- and three-spin interactions, we study an equivalent loop model in which $Q$ is a continuous parameter. By a combination of analytical and numerical arguments, we show that this loop model allows for the collision of a critical and a tricritical fixed point at $Q=4$. These then emerge as a pair of complex conformally invariant theories at $Q>4$, or even complex $Q$, for suitable complex coupling constants. We conjecture that all conformal data (such as the central charge, critical exponents, and three-point structure constants) can be obtained by analytic continuation of known exact results for the loop model with $Q \le 4$. This conjecture is checked, both for real $Q>4$ and for $Q \in \mathbb{C}$, by extensive transfer-matrix computations and comparison to previous studies for $Q=5$.
summary: This paper investigates the complex Conformal Field Theory associated with the 2D Q-state Potts model, extending its analysis beyond the standard physical regime ($Q \le 4$). By treating $Q$ as a continuous or complex variable, the authors propose that CFT data can be found through analytic continuation of known results. This work is significant for mapping out the full theoretical landscape of this critical system.
main_problem: The study aims to extend the understanding of Conformal Field Theories (CFTs) associated with the two-dimensional Q-state Potts model into regimes where the number of states, Q, is greater than 4 or complex.
main_result: The authors conjecture that all conformal data for this extended regime can be obtained by analytic continuation from known exact results for $Q \le 4$, establishing a framework for complex CFTs in this model.
method: The research combines analytical derivations, numerical transfer-matrix computations, and advanced techniques like minigrid extrapolation to map out the parameter space of the associated CFTs.
model_or_system: The system is the two-dimensional Q-state Potts model defined on a triangular lattice, which is reformulated into an equivalent loop model whose partition function allows for continuous variation of $Q$.
key_observables: Central charge ($c$), critical exponents, three-point structure constants ($\omega$), and the location of fixed points ($z_c$).
important_parameters: The number of states, Q (treated as a complex variable), and the lattice size $L$ (used for extrapolation).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the CFT data can be obtained via analytic continuation from the well-understood regime where $Q \le 4$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate paths in the complex Q-plane, convergence of extrapolated parameters ($z_c, c, \omega$) as $L 	o \infty$, and stability domains defined by conformal dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the model's fixed points across different Q regimes (real vs. complex), develops mathematical tools using transfer matrices and CFT techniques (like Dotsenko-Fateev formulas), and concludes with extensive numerical extrapolation of critical parameters.
why_interesting: While focused on statistical mechanics, the rigorous mapping to CFTs provides deep insights into universality classes and non-unitary theories, which share mathematical structures relevant to open quantum systems and boundary physics.
